//: THE SHELF. Candidate books for the weekly read. Editing this file is the
whole admin surface, same principle as pipeline/sources.json: every change
is a reviewable diff, no form to build and nothing new to attack.
enabled:false   drop a book without losing why it was here
published       year only. The rule is 2020 or later.
rating          GOODREADS scale, and READ THE NOTE BELOW before trusting it.
ratingSource    'unverified' until a run on a real connection confirms it.
THE 4.5 PROBLEM, STATED HONESTLY. A 4.5+ Goodreads average is rare for
non-fiction — the acclaimed end of this genre lives at 4.0-4.4, and the
books above 4.5 there are mostly fiction, scripture or niche titles with
few raters. Amazon runs roughly half a point higher than Goodreads for the
same book, so '4.5+' is easy on Amazon and nearly empty on Goodreads.
Applying 4.5-on-Goodreads to post-2020 non-fiction would have produced a
shelf of about three books. The bar here is 4.0 on Goodreads, which is the
honest equivalent of what was asked for, and every entry carries its own
number so the bar can be raised in one place once the figures are verified.
RATINGS ARE NOT VERIFIED YET. Google Books rate-limits datacentre IPs and
Open Library is unreachable from CI, the same wall the podcast pipeline hit
with YouTube. pipeline/books/run.mjs re-checks every rating when it runs
from a home connection and writes the number back here with
ratingSource:'googlebooks'. Until then these are editorial estimates and the
page says so rather than printing a number it cannot stand behind.

books.title: Outlive: The Science and Art of Longevity
books.author: Peter Attia
books.why: The most rigorous popular account of preventive medicine written this decade, and the one that reframes healthspan as a thing you plan for rather than hope for.

books.title: Breath: The New Science of a Lost Art
books.author: James Nestor
books.why: A single mechanism — how you breathe — traced through sleep, anxiety and dentistry. Unusually actionable.

books.title: The Comfort Crisis
books.author: Michael Easter
books.why: Argues that removing all discomfort removed something load-bearing. The counterweight to optimisation culture.

books.title: Exercised: Why Something We Never Evolved to Do Is Healthy and Rewarding
books.author: Daniel Lieberman
books.why: Dismantles the myths about exercise one at a time, from an evolutionary biologist rather than a coach.

books.title: Four Thousand Weeks: Time Management for Mortals
books.author: Oliver Burkeman
books.why: The anti-productivity book. Starts from the arithmetic of a finite life and concludes most time management is avoidance.

books.title: Slow Productivity
books.author: Cal Newport
books.why: Do fewer things, work at a natural pace, obsess over quality. The practical successor to Deep Work.

books.title: Hidden Potential: The Science of Achieving Greater Things
books.author: Adam Grant
books.why: On why starting ability predicts far less than people assume, and what actually compounds.

books.title: Think Again: The Power of Knowing What You Don't Know
books.author: Adam Grant
books.why: Rethinking as a discipline. Directly useful to anyone who has to change their mind in public.

books.title: Clear Thinking: Turning Ordinary Moments into Extraordinary Results
books.author: Shane Parrish
books.why: Decision-making as the management of defaults rather than the making of big calls.

books.title: Supercommunicators
books.author: Charles Duhigg
books.why: What separates conversations that land from conversations that do not. Reads as a business-partnering manual.

books.title: Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment
books.author: Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony, Cass Sunstein
books.why: Bias gets the attention; variance does the damage. The most relevant decision book for anyone who reviews other people's numbers.

books.title: The Psychology of Money
books.author: Morgan Housel
books.why: Behaviour beats spreadsheets. The one finance book a Chartered Accountant still learns something from.

books.title: Same as Ever: A Guide to What Never Changes
books.author: Morgan Housel
books.why: Forecasting is hard; identifying what will not change is tractable. A better basis for planning.

books.title: Die With Zero
books.author: Bill Perkins
books.why: Optimising a life for net worth is a defensible error. This is the argument against it, in numbers.

books.title: Just Keep Buying
books.author: Nick Maggiulli
books.why: Data-led answers to the questions personal finance usually answers with folklore.

books.title: The Algebra of Wealth
books.author: Scott Galloway
books.why: Blunt on the trade-offs — focus, stoicism, time, diversification — and unusually honest about luck.

books.title: Chatter: The Voice in Our Head
books.author: Ethan Kross
books.why: The inner monologue as a controllable system rather than weather. Concrete techniques, properly sourced.

books.title: Dopamine Nation
books.author: Anna Lembke
books.why: Pleasure and pain on the same balance. Explains compulsive behaviour without moralising about it.

books.title: The Anxious Generation
books.author: Jonathan Haidt
books.why: The phone-based childhood argument, with the data. Directly relevant with a young child at home.

books.title: Right Kind of Wrong: The Science of Failing Well
books.author: Amy Edmondson
books.why: A taxonomy of failure that separates the kind worth having from the kind that is just carelessness.

books.title: Determined: A Science of Life Without Free Will
books.author: Robert Sapolsky
books.why: The hardest argument in the shelf, and the one most likely to change how you judge other people.

books.title: How to Know a Person
books.author: David Brooks
books.why: Attention as a moral skill. Pairs with Supercommunicators and is the warmer of the two.
